title: Tenali Raman Tale 85

full_text:
An elderly blind beggar named Suradas sat daily outside the temple gates of Vijayanagara, singing devotional hymns. Over twenty years of frugal living, he had saved forty silver coins in a small leather pouch, which he kept tied securely around his waist to buy food in his old age.

One afternoon, while Suradas was praying, a greedy butcher named Kasim noticed the pouch, sliced the cord with his meat knife, and snatched the purse!
Suradas cried out, grabbing Kasim’s coat.
The butcher shouted: 'Liar! This is my purse! I earned these forty silver coins selling mutton in my shop today!'
Because the beggar was blind and had no witnesses, the temple guards brought both men before Tenali Raman.

Kasim swore: 'The money is mine! Why should a blind beggar have forty silver coins?'
Suradas wept: 'I saved them coin by coin for twenty years, master!'

Tenali looked at the leather purse.
He called for a large, shallow bowl of pure, boiling hot water.
Tenali untied the purse and emptied the forty silver coins straight into the steaming hot water!

Tenali, the King, and the assembly watched the surface of the water intently.
If the coins had belonged to a butcher who handled meat and animal fat all day, greasy oil droplets and fat residues would immediately rise to the surface of the hot water, forming a slick film.
However, the surface of the water remained crystal clear! Not a single droplet of grease appeared!

Instead, a faint, sweet, unmistakable fragrance of temple incense, crushed jasmine petals, and camphor rose with the steam from the hot water!
The coins had been stored for years in the beggar’s cloth beside the temple incense burners!

Tenali smiled and pointed to the clear, fragrant water:
'The coins have given their testimony!
Money from a butcher shop carries the grease of animal fat; money saved outside a temple carries the fragrance of incense and flowers!
These coins never saw a butcher's stall!'

Faced with this undeniable forensic proof, the butcher confessed his crime.
The King ordered the butcher fined eighty silver coins—which were given to Suradas—and sentenced the thief to three months of community labor.
Suradas wept tears of gratitude, praising Tenali Raman as the living eyes of justice for the blind.
moral: Forensic examination of coins reveals their recent history; truth defends the defenseless against ruthless theft.
